There's a neat story as to why I'm both. Well, neat to me anyway. I was raised in a military lodge #82 at Incirlik AB Turkey. After I left the military I moved back to my home town, and after a few years decided to get back into the craft. Oddly enough, I went to the Freemasonry subreddit for advice when I did. Turns out the Grand lodge of VA doesn't recognize the regularity of Washington State Prince Hall Masonry though, so if I wanted to join the lodge in my hometown, I was going to have to start all over. I was a bit resentful about it at fist, but my new lodge was pretty cool about it. They paid my initial fees for me, and they offered me the one day conferral. I decided to just go through all the degrees again though. Mostly because the one day conferral isn't until the end of the year, and I figured I could do it faster this way. Plus it's been so long, and the degrees are a bit different here, so I figured it couldn't hurt to relearn it all as I go. I've memorized my FC catechism, and I go up for proficiency on Thursday. I should be raised an MM again before the month is out, if all goes according to plan. I'm pretty excited to get back into it. it's been a long road to get back here.
Hey Bothers! Pleased to meet you! I'm a Prince Hall MM and a AFAM FC from VA.

That's interesting. Without going into too much detail, how different are both sides? My state does not recognize prince hall masonry either but I hope that will change someday. I'm impressed that you decided to do both.

Thanks! I'm glad I did both as well. And there's a lot of differences, although I can't tell if the difference come from it being a Prince hall lodge, or because it was a military lodge. I think the slight difference in the wording of the ceremonies come from the fact that it was PHA. But the biggest differences I'v found come from the way that EAs and FCs are treated. Here I'm treated very well, and as a brother. There we were treated not poorly, per se; well yeah, kinda poorly. But it was a military mindset. We had to earn the right to be MMs. After we went through the "gauntlet", we were accepted with open arms.

A lot of the wording varies heavily from state to state here too. Masonry is kind of the same basic story, just written by different authors. One of my favorite things to do is see other lodges do work. I've known some PHA brothers who said it was along the same lines with how they were treated as EA and FC. We have a lot of different PHA lodges in my state and as far as I know they do things differently in each one.

1 10oz. can of diced tomatoes and green chilies, mostly drained
1 3oz bag of real bacon bits
1c mayonnaise
1c shredded cheese
3 packages of mini fillo shells

Combine diced tomatoes and chilies, bacon bits, mayo, and shredded cheese in bowl until evenly mixed.

Fill mini fillo shells with mixture and place on cookie sheet, spread evenly.

Bake in preheated oven at 350oF for 15 minutes.

For brands, I typically use RoTel for the tomatoes and Athens for the mini fillo shells.

You can use any shredded cheese but I prefer Colby and Monterey Jack. I have also made my own bacon bits by frying enough bacon and then crumbling it, but that is alot of time and effort. Its better, but not enough to justify the extra effort.
